extracted.intended_audience: Australian public, government policymakers, stakeholders and interested parties
extracted.subtask_description: An informational overview of the Australian Productivity Commission: its purpose, guiding principles, core functions, topical work streams, governance and key publications. Useful for understanding the Commission's remit and how it operates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quality independent advice and information
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide quality independent advice and information to governments and communicate ideas and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as the Commission's primary contribution: supplying high-quality, independent analysis and communicating findings to governments and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating principles: independence, transparency and community-wide perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Our contribution to public debate and policy formulation is underpinned by our independence, transparency and community-wide perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three values (independence, transparency, community-wide perspective) are presented as the foundational principles guiding how the Commission operates and constructs its work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core function: inquiries and advice requested by government
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five main functions: inquiries and advice requested by government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission conducts inquiries at the government's request and provides advice based on those inquiries; this is a primary statutory/operational role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core function: Commission-initiated research
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five main functions: Commission-initiated research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission undertakes its own research projects independent of government requests, informing policy debates and long‑run strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core function: ongoing performance monitoring and benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five main functions: ongoing performance monitoring and benchmarking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission monitors and benchmarks performance (presumably of sectors, programs or service delivery) as an ongoing activity to inform analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core function: competitive neutrality complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five main functions: competitive neutrality complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling complaints about competitive neutrality is listed as a formal role of the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core function: safeguard action investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five main functions: safeguard action investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations relating to safeguard actions (likely trade or market safeguards) are a discrete function of the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work stream: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Stream
rubrics_metrics.description: One of seven work streams: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Stream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies Indigenous policy and related issues as an explicit topical focus area for the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work stream: Climate Change and Energy
rubrics_metrics.description: One of seven work streams: Climate Change and Energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Climate and energy policy is an explicit thematic area of the Commission's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work stream: Data and Digital
rubrics_metrics.description: One of seven work streams: Data and Digital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data and digital policy issues are a named focus for research and advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work stream: Environment and Water
rubrics_metrics.description: One of seven work streams: Environment and Water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental and water resource policy are explicit topic streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work stream: Health and Ageing
rubrics_metrics.description: One of seven work streams: Health and Ageing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health and ageing policy is identified as a thematic area for the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work stream: Industry and Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: One of seven work streams: Industry and Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry and trade policy issues are a named area of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work stream: Productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: One of seven work streams: Productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Productivity (broad economic productivity issues) is a core thematic focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance commitment: accountability and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The PC is committed to accountability and transparency by publishing procedures and other legal documents in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission frames publishing procedures and legal documents as part of its governance and accountability obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Report: details of operations and reflection on research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annual Report provides details of the PC’s operations and reflects on current research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reporting is presented as a key accountability product documenting operations and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate Plan: strategic direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate plan provides strategic direction to guide our activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corporate plan is identified as the forward-looking document that guides the Commission's activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis: established under the Productivity Commission Act 1998
rubrics_metrics.description: The PC was established under the Productivity Commission Act 1998.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act is cited as the statutory foundation for the Commission's existence and functions.
